concepts.way: misconception: local variables get a default value on their own
concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: The answer says declaring a local variable sets it to 0, but in Java a local declared without an initializer has no value, and reading it is a compile error.
The answer only says c is 0 because it was declared, which is a mistake about declaration, not about int; it says nothing about int itself, such as its range or how int arithmetic works.

concepts.way: misconception: local variables get a default value on their own
concepts.why: The answer treats an unassigned local variable as holding 0, which goes against the rule that a variable must be assigned before it is read.
The answer says nothing about double.
